subject: accordion
pitch:
Category: Object.
Subject: piano accordion.
Style: Italian mother-of-pearl.
reasoning:
I'm planning the accordion model's overall structure and dimensions, deciding it should stand roughly 0.45m wide with the body resting on the floor, and working out how to orient the keyboard and bass sides.

I'll place the keyboard on the front face with keys extending outward from the bellows, stacked vertically — about 17 white keys sized to fit the 0.42 box height, with shorter black keys between. For the bodies, I'm planning alternating pleats for the bellows and a mother-of-pearl palette with pale pink, blue, and mint iridescent tones against black lacquer trim and chrome/gold accents.

I'm settling on pearl celluloid for the body with black bellows edged in white pearl pleats and gold trim, chrome grille details, and small rubber feet to support the boxes off the ground. Now I'm writing a simple box-building helper to construct each static part (treble box, bass box, bellows folds) with position, size, and color, starting with the treble box dimensions.

For the keyboard, I'm laying out white keys as thin boxes spaced along the front face of the treble box, and figuring out placement for the shorter black keys relative to them.

I'm also planning the treble box details: the pearl top cap with ornament, the side grille or plain surface option, the register switch block near the top, and framing around the keyboard. Then I'm moving to the bass box, mirroring the treble's position and size, and thinking through how the bass buttons should be oriented on their face.

For straps, I'm keeping it simple: a plain dark panel for the buttons, and basic strap boxes swept across the back of both bass and treble sides for the hand loops.

Now I'm working out the bellows structure — alternating pleats across the width, deciding between uniform or varying peak/valley dimensions and colors to mimic the folded accordion look.

I'm planning to add pearl corner caps at each peak (four per peak, seven peaks) plus a front strap with a chrome buckle connecting the bass and treble boxes across the bellows.

Now I'm adding chrome edging strips along the box edges, trim bands on the top and bottom lids, eight small gold corner spheres, and diamond-shaped pearl inlays—keeping the treble end plain but giving the bass end a mosaic grid of varied pearl-colored tiles.

Simplifying the mosaic to a 4x8 grid of 32 small colored boxes, adding black cylinder feet, and considering a gold logo plate on the treble front and a bass button board panel. I'm now drafting the specific placement requests—position, orientation, and room dimensions—for the treble grille (chrome perforated with pearl-pink scrollwork) and the register switches.

Continuing with placements: bass buttons sized as rows with pearl caps, and the brand plate positioned above the keyboard on the treble front since the bellows surface would flex too much. I'm fitting it into the gap between the keyboard top and frame top, then moving on to figure out the gold bellows corners.

I'm deciding to skip building actual straps and buckles myself, instead specifying them as separate leather shoulder straps and a bass wrist strap in the request to keep things simpler. For decorative touches, I'm planning pearl inlay accents near the bass end rather than full corner rosettes.

Since pearl is core to this accordion's aesthetic, I'll build some of the pearl paneling myself—alternating colored pearl tiles bordering the keyboard area—but leave finer shimmer textures and additional inlay detailing to the request rather than modeling every tile. I'll keep key labels simple and skip elaborate key decor for now.

I'm placing the air release button on the bass top and defining the texture set: pearl shimmer for the body shells, a paper-pleat pattern for the bellows, ivory grain for the white keys, and engraved trim for the chrome edges. For part naming, I'll give the body shells distinct names like "trebleBody" and "bassBody," and let the repeated bellows peaks share a name since sequential auto-naming should handle uniqueness fine.

Writing box geometry and layout code...

Adding trim details now: black lid strips top and bottom of each box, chrome edge strips at front corners, and gold corner studs as small spheres. Now working out bellows peak positions along x.

Adding strips only at front/back for the caps, then sketching a dark bass box front panel. I'm finalizing the color palette—pearl tones, lacquer, chrome, gold, ivory, key black—and deciding bellows valleys should use a red tone for an Italian-style pearl-and-red look.

Now I'm working out pearl inlay placement: adding rotated diamond lozenge plates to the box tops, but realizing the treble top needs to stay clear for register switches. I'm resolving the conflict by putting the pink pearl lozenge only on the bass top, keeping the treble top open for switches and a brand plate.

Now I'm finalizing the design with pearl lozenges added to the treble back panel too, then writing out the export code with the builder setup, metadata, requests, and stage2 definitions.
